title: Inflation Is Way Down. Is It by Design or Just Luck?

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店里用黑胶唱片打碟的那个年代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着 300 件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，把 DJ 台变成一个充满 50 年前精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼带来的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, after two years of record high consumer prices, inflation is falling in a big way.
sentences.zh: 今天，在经历了两年创纪录的高消费价格后，通货膨胀正在大幅下降。

sentences.en: The question now being asked by economists, according to my colleague Gina Smilic, is whether that's by design or by accident.
sentences.zh: 据我的同事吉娜·斯米利克称，经济学家们现在提出的问题是，这到底是政策使然，还是纯属巧合。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, June 20th.
sentences.zh: 今天是 6 月 20 日，星期二。

sentences.en: Good morning, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家早上好。

sentences.en: This is a big day.
sentences.zh: 今天是个大日子。

sentences.en: New inflation numbers and, yeah, your money's at stake.
sentences.zh: 新的通胀数据出炉了，没错，这关系到你的钱袋子。

sentences.en: Here we go.
sentences.zh: 我们开始吧。

sentences.en: New economic numbers showing inflation is easing up.
sentences.zh: 新的经济数据显示通胀正在缓解。

sentences.en: 4% inflation at the consumer level.
sentences.zh: 消费者层面的通胀率为 4%。

sentences.en: Much slower than the 9% that we had seen in the summer of last year was.
sentences.zh: 比我们去年夏天看到的 9% 要慢得多。

sentences.en: We know the goal is down.
sentences.zh: 我们知道目标是降下来。

sentences.en: How down is this?
sentences.zh: 这降幅到底有多少？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This is down.
sentences.zh: 确实降了。

sentences.en: This is the slowest pace in two years.
sentences.zh: 这是两年来最慢的增速。

sentences.en: We're getting there just very slowly.
sentences.zh: 我们正在实现目标，只是速度非常缓慢。

sentences.en: Fed meets tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 美联储明天开会。

sentences.en: Big decision coming.
sentences.zh: 重大决策即将出炉。

sentences.en: In light of how far we've come in tightening policy, today we decided to leave our policy interest rate unchanged.
sentences.zh: 鉴于我们在收紧政策方面已经走了这么远，今天我们决定维持政策利率不变。

sentences.en: The Federal Reserve hit the pause button today on hiking interest rates as it tries to tame inflation.
sentences.zh: 美联储今天按下了加息的暂停键，试图以此抑制通胀。

sentences.en: That is a significant shift after 10 straight meetings where they raised interest rates.
sentences.zh: 在连续 10 次会议加息之后，这是一个重大的转变。

sentences.en: This is a really important moment for the economy and for the Federal Reserve.
sentences.zh: 这对经济和美联储来说都是一个非常重要的时刻。

sentences.en: It has been on this mission where it's...
sentences.zh: 它一直肩负着这样的使命，那就是……

sentences.en: Gina, good morning.
sentences.zh: 吉娜，早上好。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: We wanted to talk to you as our resident inflation expert because it now feels that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我们想以我们常驻通胀专家的身份和你聊聊，因为现在感觉美国

sentences.en: government's long-term plan to try to lower inflation by raising the interest rate month after month after month is working.
sentences.zh: 政府通过月复一月地提高利率来降低通胀的长期计划正在奏效。

sentences.en: And it feels that way for two reasons.
sentences.zh: 而且有两个原因让人有这种感觉。

sentences.en: The first is that a few days ago we got data showing that monthly inflation is now less than half of what it was last summer.
sentences.zh: 首先是几天前我们得到的数据显示，现在的月度通胀率已经不到去年夏天的一半了。

sentences.en: It's a really big decline.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常大的降幅。

sentences.en: And right on cue a day later, the Federal Reserve decided to pause its program of raising interest rates, which seemed to confirm the idea that inflation is in retreat.
sentences.zh: 紧接着一天后，美联储就决定暂停加息计划，这似乎证实了通胀正在消退的观点。

sentences.en: And so we come to you, Gina, to ask, are we correct to understand that the government's policies are slaying the inflationary beast?
sentences.zh: 所以我们来问问你，吉娜，我们理解政府的政策正在扼杀通胀猛兽，这种说法对吗？

sentences.en: So I can totally see why you would think that, because inflation has fallen quite a bit, and that is obviously really good news.
sentences.zh: 我完全明白你为什么会这么想，因为通胀确实下降了不少，这显然是个好消息。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But I think the key question here and the question you're asking is whether policy is responsible.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这里的关键问题，也是你正在问的问题，是政策是否起到了决定性作用。

sentences.en: And the answer to that one is pretty complicated right now.
sentences.zh: 而这个问题的答案目前相当复杂。

sentences.en: The way I like to think about this is that we're really in a story where we're talking about luck on one hand and policy on the other.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这样思考：我们实际上处于一个既有运气成分，又有政策影响的故事中。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: That's a great-sounding framework, luck versus policy.
sentences.zh: 这是一个听起来很棒的框架，运气与政策。

sentences.en: Explain it.
sentences.zh: 解释一下。

sentences.en: It means basically what it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 意思基本就如其字面所言。

sentences.en: Some of the decline in inflation that we're seeing is a result of policy from the Federal Reserve.
sentences.zh: 我们所看到的通胀下降，有一部分是美联储政策的结果。

sentences.en: But a lot of it is luck, which is to say that raising interest rates had little or nothing to do with it.
sentences.zh: 但很大程度上是运气，也就是说，加息与此几乎没什么关系。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Give us an example of luck-based inflation decline.
sentences.zh: 给我们举一个运气驱动通胀下降的例子。

sentences.en: So I think that there are really two big areas that have experienced significant declines in inflation that had to do with luck or the way the world was expected to play out,
sentences.zh: 我认为有两个主要领域经历了显著的通胀下降，这与运气或世界预期的发展方式有关，

sentences.en: rather than purely sort of the policy response to inflation.
sentences.zh: 而不是纯粹的通胀政策应对。

sentences.en: Gas and groceries.
sentences.zh: 汽油和食品杂货。

sentences.en: Two very big categories of expense in life.
sentences.zh: 生活中两项非常大的开支类别。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so I think gas is a good place to start.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为汽油是一个很好的切入点。

sentences.en: It really started to jump over the last couple of summers.
sentences.zh: 过去几个夏天，油价确实开始飙升。

sentences.en: And you probably remember, you know, when a gallon of gas cost something like $5 just for regular at the pump.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得，当时每加仑普通汽油的价格大约要 5 美元。

sentences.en: I very, very well remember it because it turns into like a $70 tank of gas.
sentences.zh: 我记得非常清楚，因为加满一箱油要 70 美元左右。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It was really painful for consumers.
sentences.zh: 这对消费者来说真的很痛苦。

sentences.en: And that's come down by a lot.
sentences.zh: 现在价格已经大幅下降了。

sentences.en: It's now like $3.59 a gallon.
sentences.zh: 现在每加仑大约是 3.59 美元。

sentences.en: Similarly, for groceries, you probably remember that eggs, for instance, four or five months ago were something like $5 a dozen.
sentences.zh: 同样，对于食品杂货，你可能记得四五个月前，比如鸡蛋，一打大约要 5 美元。

sentences.en: And they're now down quite a bit to something more like $2.50.
sentences.zh: 现在已经降了不少，大约是 2.50 美元。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: 50% decline.
sentences.zh: 下降了 50%。

sentences.en: Very meaningful.
sentences.zh: 非常有意义。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so those are big declines, but they aren't necessarily categories that are sort of rooted in the Fed's policy response.
sentences.zh: 所以这些都是巨大的降幅，但它们并不一定属于美联储政策应对的范畴。

sentences.en: Really, what we're seeing here is the sort of result of some big outside events.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我们在这里看到的是一些重大外部事件的结果。

sentences.en: Why don't you start with gas?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不从汽油开始讲起呢？

sentences.en: I mean, why is the decline in gas pretty much unrelated to federal policy and much more in the realm of luck?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为什么汽油价格的下降与联邦政策几乎无关，而更多属于运气的范畴？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So just in general, changes in oil and gas prices are almost always the result of sort of big global trends.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，石油和天然气价格的变化几乎总是全球大趋势的结果。

sentences.en: Decisions made by Russia, decisions made by Saudi Arabia, the speed of growth in other big economies like China.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯的决定、沙特阿拉伯的决定，以及中国等其他大经济体的增长速度。

sentences.en: And so those things sort of move the price of gas around.
sentences.zh: 这些因素在一定程度上左右了油价。

sentences.en: You can get some domestic policies, like some things the White House can do can matter to oil prices around the edges.
sentences.zh: 你可能会看到一些国内政策，比如白宫采取的一些措施可能会在边缘地带影响油价。

sentences.en: But mostly this is sort of this big external force acting on the economy.
sentences.zh: 但主要还是这种巨大的外部力量在作用于经济。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So not really because of federal policy?
sentences.zh: 所以并不是因为联邦政策？

sentences.en: Not primarily.
sentences.zh: 主要不是。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And what about the big declines in grocery prices?
sentences.zh: 那食品杂货价格的大幅下降呢？

sentences.en: Why do we not attribute that to rising interest rates?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不把它归因于加息？

sentences.en: So I think we can start with egg prices, which we've previously talked about.
sentences.zh: 我们可以从我们之前谈过的鸡蛋价格开始说起。

sentences.en: So we obviously know that egg prices spiked really high earlier this year in January.
sentences.zh: 我们显然知道，今年早些时候，也就是一月份，鸡蛋价格飙升得非常高。

sentences.en: They hit that $5 mark almoSt.
sentences.zh: 几乎达到了 5 美元大关。

sentences.en: And that was really about bad luck.
sentences.zh: 那纯粹是运气不好。

sentences.en: We had a really bad bout of avian flu that was killing millions of chickens.
sentences.zh: 我们经历了一场非常严重的禽流感，导致数百万只鸡死亡。

sentences.en: And so chicken prices jumped, egg prices jumped.
sentences.zh: 所以鸡肉价格上涨了，鸡蛋价格也上涨了。

sentences.en: But more recently, that's really started to clear up, which has been good luck.
sentences.zh: 但最近情况已经开始好转，这算是好运气。

sentences.en: And so it's helped to bring prices down.
sentences.zh: 这有助于价格回落。

sentences.en: And this is sort of what you see with food overall.
sentences.zh: 这就是你在整体食品价格上看到的情况。

sentences.en: By and large, when we think about things like food prices, we often think that they are pretty sensitive to big movements in commodity prices, in grain prices, in dairy prices.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，当我们考虑食品价格这类事物时，我们通常认为它们对大宗商品价格、谷物价格、乳制品价格的剧烈波动非常敏感。

sentences.en: And so they're just not good as a clear read on where the economy is headed or how policy is working.
sentences.zh: 所以它们不能很好地反映经济走向或政策效果。

sentences.en: Right, because the Fed does not eradicate avian flu.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为美联储无法根除禽流感。

sentences.en: It does not spare the lives of chickens.
sentences.zh: 它也无法拯救鸡的生命。

sentences.en: So this is not a good measure of policy working.
sentences.zh: 所以这不是衡量政策是否奏效的好指标。

sentences.en: Like you said, it's a measure of kind of agrarian luck.
sentences.zh: 就像你说的，这是一种农业运气的衡量标准。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You're not going to get a clean assessment off of food prices.
sentences.zh: 你无法从食品价格中得到清晰的评估。

sentences.en: So very interestingly, Gina, the decline of inflation in these two big areas where higher prices most directly impact us as consumers,
sentences.zh: 所以非常有趣的是，吉娜，通胀在这些我们消费者最直接感受到价格上涨的两个大领域出现下降，

sentences.en: it's not primarily because our central bank worked its magic, but the overall impact is that inflation is really down.
sentences.zh: 这并不是因为我们的央行施展了魔法，但总体影响是通胀确实下降了。

sentences.en: Yes, inflation is really down.
sentences.zh: 是的，通胀确实下降了。

sentences.en: And another reason that overall inflation is down so much is because we've really seen a lot of healing in supply chains,
sentences.zh: 整体通胀下降如此之多的另一个原因是，我们确实看到了供应链的极大修复，

sentences.en: which, as listeners probably remember, got really messed up during and after the coronavirus pandemic and which have been slowly getting back to normal.
sentences.zh: 听众朋友们可能还记得，供应链在新冠疫情期间及之后变得一团糟，现在正慢慢恢复正常。

sentences.en: So the part of inflation we're worried about now is the part that's not going to come down just because of a return to normal or because of luck,
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在担心的那部分通胀，不是那种仅仅因为恢复正常或运气好就会下降的部分，

sentences.en: but the part that is going to require Fed policy.
sentences.zh: 而是需要美联储政策介入的那部分。

sentences.en: And we're seeing Fed policies start to work in some categories, but in many categories, we're not seeing that much progress yet.
sentences.zh: 我们看到美联储的政策在某些领域开始奏效，但在许多领域，我们还没有看到太大的进展。

sentences.en: But we're seeing this sort of split screen story in the economy where it is certainly the case that some big areas of inflation are moderating.
sentences.zh: 但我们正在经济中看到这种“分屏”现象，即某些大的通胀领域确实在放缓，这是事实。

sentences.en: But at the same time, we've got some other big areas that haven't budged very much.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，还有其他一些大的领域几乎没有动静。

sentences.en: And that's why, despite inflation cooling down so much over the past few months, we still can't say that we've slayed the inflationary beaSt.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么尽管过去几个月通胀降温不少，我们仍然不能说已经扼杀了通胀猛兽。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33 位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 430 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨 4 点 30 分给总统打电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 七十年的太空探索。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费者产品指南。

sentences.en: Today, I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天，我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60 款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎每年都是联盟中最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝 175 年来帮助你了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享受 nytimes.com/subscribe 上的特别优惠。

sentences.en: Gina, right before the break, you said that there are areas where the Federal Reserve's policy is starting to do what it's supposed to do, which is lower inflation,
sentences.zh: 吉娜，在休息之前，你说过有些领域美联储的政策开始发挥应有的作用，即降低通胀，

sentences.en: despite the fact that in a lot of areas it can't quite make that happen.
sentences.zh: 尽管在很多领域它还无法做到这一点。

sentences.en: So I want to zero in on the areas where Fed policy is working.
sentences.zh: 所以我想重点关注美联储政策奏效的领域。

sentences.en: So what's an example of that?
sentences.zh: 那有什么例子吗？

sentences.en: So the one I would come back to most often, I think, is rents.
sentences.zh: 我想我最常提到的一个例子是租金。

sentences.en: So there was a while back in really the summer of 21 and into the spring of 2022 where rent increases were just crazy.
sentences.zh: 在 2021 年夏天到 2022 年春天的那段时间里，租金涨幅简直疯狂。

sentences.en: If you live in New York, you probably remember, you know, rent was going up so faSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你住在纽约，你可能还记得，租金涨得太快了。

sentences.en: This was like brunch conversation.
sentences.zh: 这简直是早午餐时的谈资。

sentences.en: The rents were so quick.
sentences.zh: 租金涨得太快了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is like the story of the $6,000 one bedrooMs.
sentences.zh: 这就像是 6000 美元一居室的故事。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And that was really, really bad news on the inflation front because rents make up just a huge chunk of the inflation calculation.
sentences.zh: 这在通胀方面确实是个非常糟糕的消息，因为租金在通胀计算中占了很大一部分。

sentences.en: The good news here is that rents have really slowed down in the market.
sentences.zh: 这里的好消息是，市场上的租金确实放缓了。

sentences.en: So what we're seeing is that sort of real-time data providers are telling us that for basically the past year, rents have been much slower to rise.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的是，实时数据提供商告诉我们，基本上在过去一年里，租金上涨速度慢多了。

sentences.en: And so that should really help to allow overall inflation to cool.
sentences.zh: 所以这应该真的有助于整体通胀降温。

sentences.en: And that is probably a little bit of a Fed story.
sentences.zh: 这可能在一定程度上归功于美联储。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: How do we know that?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么知道？

sentences.en: So one of the big ways in which rents are a Fed story is that they very closely track what's happening in the labor market and how confident people are feeling.
sentences.zh: 租金与美联储相关的一个重要方式是，它们与劳动力市场的情况以及人们的信心密切相关。

sentences.en: So if you're making better wages, if you're feeling confident you're going to get that new job and you're going to get a raise because everyone loves you at work,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你工资更高，如果你确信自己能找到新工作，并且因为大家在工作中都喜欢你而能获得加薪，

sentences.en: you're going to feel much more comfortable springing for that jacuzzi bathtub and taking on the slightly higher rent that comes alongside it.
sentences.zh: 你就会觉得为了那个按摩浴缸而多花点钱，并承担随之而来的略高租金，心里会踏实得多。

sentences.en: And so rents can be, in a way, a sort of economic sentiment indicator, or at least they're very closely connected.
sentences.zh: 所以租金在某种程度上可以算是一种经济情绪指标，或者至少它们之间有着非常紧密的联系。

sentences.en: And so I think that if you want to point to a clear place where Fed policy is working, that's probably it.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，如果你想找出一个美联储政策确实奏效的明确领域，那可能就是租金。

sentences.en: So just to be sure I understand this, Gina, when interest rates go up, as they have now for many, many months,
sentences.zh: 为了确保我理解得没错，吉娜，当利率上升时，就像现在这样已经持续了好几个月，

sentences.en: the economy starts to look a little bit less rosy to a typical worker.
sentences.zh: 普通工薪阶层眼中的经济前景就会开始变得没那么乐观了。

sentences.en: And you start to wonder if your economic prospects are going to be as strong as they once looked.
sentences.zh: 你开始怀疑自己的经济前景是否还能像过去看起来那样强劲。

sentences.en: And maybe you think twice about a long-term rental commitment, you know, a year or two years, that feels like a splurge.
sentences.zh: 也许你会对长期的租房承诺三思而后行，你知道，签个一年两年的合同，感觉就像是一种挥霍。

sentences.en: And so in that way, Fed policy raising interest rates helps lower the rental price increases that we have been seeing for so many months.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个角度来看，美联储加息有助于降低我们过去几个月一直看到的租金涨幅。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So when interest rates go up, the labor market slows down a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以当利率上升时，劳动力市场会大幅放缓。

sentences.en: And economists will often tell you that the labor market and rents are very closely related.
sentences.zh: 经济学家通常会告诉你，劳动力市场和租金之间有着非常密切的关系。

sentences.en: If your wages are going up, you feel more comfortable paying more.
sentences.zh: 如果你的工资在上涨，你就会觉得支付更高的费用也无所谓。

sentences.en: If your wages are stalling out or you're even worried that you might get laid off, you're going to feel much less comfortable paying more.
sentences.zh: 如果你的工资停滞不前，甚至担心自己可能会被裁员，你就会觉得支付更高的费用让人难以接受。

sentences.en: And your landlord just isn't going to be able to put up prices as much.
sentences.zh: 而你的房东也就没法那么大幅度地涨价了。

sentences.en: And so rents can be a good barometer of where the overall economy is heading.
sentences.zh: 所以租金可以作为衡量整体经济走向的一个很好的晴雨表。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So that's rent.
sentences.zh: 这就是租金的情况。

sentences.en: I'm curious if this phenomenon you're describing is also translating over to housing sales, not rent, but people purchasing homes, a really big, important part of the economy
sentences.zh: 我很好奇你描述的这种现象是否也转化到了房屋销售上，不是租房，而是人们买房，这是经济中非常重要的一部分，

sentences.en: where Fed policy in theory could have this desired impact of slowing things down.
sentences.zh: 理论上美联储的政策可以在这里产生预期的放缓效果。

sentences.en: So, yes, but housing is a pretty weird situation right now.
sentences.zh: 是的，但房地产市场目前的情况相当奇怪。

sentences.en: Higher interest rates absolutely did cool off the housing market last year.
sentences.zh: 更高的利率确实在去年冷却了房地产市场。

sentences.en: And sales are still pretty depressed.
sentences.zh: 而且销售额仍然相当低迷。

sentences.en: But what we're seeing is that there's some demand out there sort of lingering on the sidelines.
sentences.zh: 但我们看到的是，市场上仍有一些需求在观望。

sentences.en: And there's not a lot of supply in the housing market.
sentences.zh: 而且房地产市场的供应量并不多。

sentences.en: So while home prices actually fell late last year, they've recently started to turn around and climb again.
sentences.zh: 所以虽然房价在去年年底确实有所下跌，但最近又开始回升并再次攀升。

sentences.en: And so I think the upshot here is that the Fed did cool housing, but it hasn't exactly kept it in a deep freeze.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为结论是，美联储确实冷却了房地产市场，但并没有让它完全陷入冰封状态。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And it sounds like you're saying they would like for it to be in something resembling a deep freeze.
sentences.zh: 听起来你的意思是，他们希望它能处于某种类似于冰封的状态。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think that a deep freeze would give them confidence that they have cooled off the economy in this way that's being sustained.
sentences.zh: 我认为冰封状态会让他们确信，他们已经以一种可持续的方式冷却了经济。

sentences.en: And instead, what we're seeing is that the economy still has some oomph, despite everything that the Fed has done.
sentences.zh: 然而我们看到的是，尽管美联储做了这么多，经济依然充满活力。

sentences.en: And it's one of the reasons that in some pretty important categories, you really just haven't seen price increases come down that much.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么在一些非常重要的类别中，你确实还没看到价格有太大的回落。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because oomph is another word for prices that are a little bit higher than we'd like.
sentences.zh: 因为“活力”是价格比我们预期的要高一点的另一种说法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: If you have stronger demand, if you have that little bit of consumer oomph, it allows companies to keep raising their prices.
sentences.zh: 如果你有更强的需求，如果你有那么一点消费活力，它就能让企业继续提高价格。

sentences.en: I could just keep saying oomph all day long.
sentences.zh: 我可以整天一直说“活力”这个词。

sentences.en: But can you tell us where in the economy the prices remain stubbornly high and where, as a result, we can understand the Fed policy to have been stymied?
sentences.zh: 但你能告诉我们，经济中哪些领域的价格依然顽固地居高不下，因此我们可以认为美联储的政策在这些地方受阻了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: So one word here, services.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个词：服务业。

sentences.en: And by that, I mean stuff like child care, concert tickets, haircuts, you know, anything that you buy that's a non-physical good, that really is sort of very labor-based.
sentences.zh: 我指的是像托儿服务、音乐会门票、理发之类的东西，你知道，任何你购买的非实物商品，确实是非常依赖劳动力的那种。

sentences.en: That's sort of the area we're worried about right now.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们目前担心的领域。

sentences.en: And what's our understanding of why those categories, which like groceries and like gas, are a pretty big part of your life, right?
sentences.zh: 我们对这些类别为何如此难以通过美联储政策来压低价格有什么了解吗？毕竟它们就像杂货和汽油一样，是你生活中很大的一部分，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, why are these categories so difficult for the Fed's policy to pierce and to bring prices down on?
sentences.zh: 为什么这些类别对美联储的政策如此“免疫”？

sentences.en: So it's a couple of things simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 这是几件事同时作用的结果。

sentences.en: One is that wage growth remains relatively quick.
sentences.zh: 一是工资增长依然相对较快。

sentences.en: And that matters in two ways.
sentences.zh: 这在两个方面很重要。

sentences.en: It matters first because if, as a company, you are paying more, you are likely going to try and pass along those higher costs to your consumers in the form of higher prices.
sentences.zh: 首先，如果作为一家公司，你支付的成本更高，你很可能会试图以更高价格的形式将这些成本转嫁给消费者。

sentences.en: It also matters because if, as an American shopper, you are earning more in wages, you are likely going to be able to turn around and spend a little bit more,
sentences.zh: 其次，如果作为一名美国购物者，你的工资收入更高，你很可能能够转而多花一点钱，

sentences.en: even if you're not thrilled about it, when the company that you're buying stuff from is trying to charge you.
sentences.zh: 即使你对涨价并不高兴，但当你购买商品的公司试图向你收费时，你还是会买。

sentences.en: And so it helps to keep prices climbing.
sentences.zh: 所以这有助于维持价格的持续攀升。

sentences.en: The other thing is that corporations have gotten pretty used to charging more.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，企业已经相当习惯于提高收费了。

sentences.en: And so we're seeing a situation where they know they have a little bit of ability to push up prices, and they're doing that either to maintain or to grow their profits.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到的情况是，他们知道自己有能力推高价格，而且他们这样做是为了维持或增加利润。

sentences.en: These are sort of a bunch of trends that, you know, you and I, Michael, and you and other guests have talked about in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 这些都是一系列趋势，你知道，你和我，迈克尔，还有你和其他嘉宾过去都讨论过这些。

sentences.en: But what's surprising is that they remain true, even in spite of everything the Fed has done to cool down the economy.
sentences.zh: 但令人惊讶的是，尽管美联储为了冷却经济做了这么多，这些趋势依然存在。

sentences.en: Fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: Gina, I'm curious about something.
sentences.zh: 吉娜，我很好奇一件事。

sentences.en: If rent increases go down because workers-slash-consumers start to psychologically feel things are a little more delicate, how does that square with what you just said,
sentences.zh: 如果租金上涨是因为工薪阶层兼消费者在心理上开始感到情况变得更加微妙，那这和你刚才说的怎么吻合呢？

sentences.en: that workers-slash-consumers are feeling good enough that they're willing to pay for higher prices on things like concert tickets and haircuts?
sentences.zh: 你说工薪阶层兼消费者感觉良好，以至于他们愿意为音乐会门票和理发等东西支付更高的价格？

sentences.en: How do we make sense of that?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何理解这一点？

sentences.en: Well, if you think about it, you know, a rental agreement is really sort of a bet on the future.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你仔细想想，你知道，租赁协议实际上是对未来的一种赌注。

sentences.en: You're entering into a 12-month or 24-month agreement, and you're saying you're going to pay this amount for that entire period,
sentences.zh: 你签署了一份12个月或24个月的协议，你承诺在整个期间支付这笔金额，

sentences.en: and so you have to assess whether you're going to be able to do that.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须评估自己是否能够做到这一点。

sentences.en: Whereas, you know, a haircut or a concert ticket, you know, something that is a little bit more in the moment
sentences.zh: 而你知道，理发或音乐会门票，你知道，那种更即时的消费，

sentences.en: is really a reflection of how you're feeling about your finances just today, not looking forward to the future.
sentences.zh: 实际上反映的是你今天对财务状况的感受，而不是展望未来。

sentences.en: And so they don't have sort of that barometer of how you're feeling about your prospects embedded in them.
sentences.zh: 所以它们并没有嵌入那种关于你对未来前景感受的晴雨表。

sentences.en: Another thing we probably want to think about with rents is that you've got a certain population that's renting, and they're the people who are likely getting squeezed
sentences.zh: 关于租金，我们可能还需要考虑的另一件事是，有一部分租房群体，他们很可能是目前被通胀挤压得最厉害的人，

sentences.en: pretty severely by inflation right now.
sentences.zh: 挤压得相当严重。

sentences.en: It is the case that renters tend to skew a little bit younger.
sentences.zh: 租房者往往偏向于更年轻一点。

sentences.en: They tend to skew a little bit lower income.
sentences.zh: 他们的收入往往偏低一点。

sentences.en: And so we could see sort of a divided situation in the economy where those folks are really struggling to sustain their spending
sentences.zh: 所以我们可能会在经济中看到一种分裂的情况，那些人真的在努力维持他们的消费水平，

sentences.en: at a comfortable level and struggling to pay up more to rent the place that they want to rent.
sentences.zh: 维持在一个舒适的水平，并且在努力支付更高的租金来租到他们想要的房子。

sentences.en: Whereas we've got people who own their houses who are a little bit more financially well-off, who are a little bit older, and they're still really able to consume like crazy.
sentences.zh: 而我们有那些拥有自己房子的人，他们经济状况更好一点，年龄更大一点，他们仍然能够疯狂消费。

sentences.en: So, Gina, if you're the central bank, if you're the Fed, you're probably pretty frustrated that you can't knock some of these stubborn price increases
sentences.zh: 所以，吉娜，如果你是中央银行，如果你是美联储，你可能会感到非常沮丧，因为在经历了这么多月的加息之后，你仍然无法压下我们一直在谈论的那些顽固的价格上涨，

sentences.en: that we've been talking about down after all these months of raising interest rates, which is supposed to make borrowing more expensive, as we talked about,
sentences.zh: 正如我们所讨论的，加息本应使借贷成本更高，

sentences.en: which is supposed to cool down the economy and ultimately bring down prices.
sentences.zh: 本应冷却经济并最终降低价格。

sentences.en: And so that makes me wonder why the Federal Reserve didn't use its power to keep trying to lower inflation last week when it had the chance.
sentences.zh: 这让我很想知道，为什么美联储上周有机会时没有利用其权力继续尝试降低通胀。

sentences.en: It could have come out and said, listen, America, we still have work to do here on inflation, and so we're going to have to raise interest rates.
sentences.zh: 它本可以出来说，听着，美国，我们在通胀问题上还有工作要做，所以我们必须提高利率。

sentences.en: We just haven't gotten as far as we'd like to.
sentences.zh: 我们只是还没有达到我们想要的程度。

sentences.en: And instead, the Fed didn't do anything, which is a little bit counterintuitive given everything you've told us here.
sentences.zh: 但美联储什么也没做，考虑到你在这里告诉我们的一切，这有点违背直觉。

sentences.en: So why didn't the Fed just raise interest rates another time?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么美联储没有再加息一次呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So a couple of things here.
sentences.zh: 这里有几点原因。

sentences.en: So the Fed did not raise interest rates, but it's not exactly the case that they didn't do anything.
sentences.zh: 美联储确实没有加息，但这并不意味着他们什么都没做。

sentences.en: What the Fed did is it hit pause on interest rate increases for the first time in 11 meetings, very big deal, but it also signaled that it's going to raise rates
sentences.zh: 美联储所做的是在11次会议以来首次暂停加息，这是一件大事，但它也暗示今年还会再加息两次，这比我们预期的要多。

sentences.en: twice more this year, which is more than we had expected.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点令人惊讶。

sentences.en: And so that was a bit of a surprise.
sentences.zh: 我认为它传达的信息是，我们想在这里保持谨慎。

sentences.en: And I think that the message it sent was, we want to be cautious here.
sentences.zh: 我们想尽量不搞垮经济，但我们对通胀的走向非常担心。

sentences.en: We want to try not to blow up the economy, but we're pretty darn worried about where inflation is headed.
sentences.zh: 我认为美联储决定现在暂停，并承诺以后做更多或暗示他们可能会做更多，是因为我们最近非常担心银行业的动荡。

sentences.en: And the reason I think that the Fed decided to hit pause now and promise to do more or suggest that they might do more later is that we've been pretty worried
sentences.zh: 美联储曾暗示，在看到一系列银行在利率上升中倒闭后，它可能会暂停一下，环顾四周，尝试评估其已经采取的行动是如何发挥作用的。

sentences.en: about banking turmoil recently.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是谨慎行事的部分原因。

sentences.en: The Fed had suggested that it might sort of take a pause, look around, try and assess how the moves it's already made were playing out after we saw a bunch of banks blow up
sentences.zh: 我认为谨慎行事的部分原因仅仅是因为美联储已经做了很多了。

sentences.en: amid rising interest rates.
sentences.zh: 所以它想放慢脚步，以确保他们能实现软着陆，即他们做了足够多的工作来控制通胀，但又不会做得太过火，

sentences.en: And so I think that that was part of the reason for the caution.
sentences.zh: 以至于在这个过程中彻底摧毁了经济。

sentences.en: And I think part of the reason for the caution is just the Fed has done a lot already.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so it kind of wants to slow walk this to try and make sure that they sort of nail the landing here, that they do enough to get inflation under control, but not so much
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这次暂停加息并不是说，嘿，我们现在状况很好。

sentences.en: that they absolutely tank the economy in the process.
sentences.zh: 我们已经度过了难关。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 这次暂停是在说，让我们确保一年左右后我们还有一个银行业。

sentences.en: In other words, this was not a pause in raising interest rates that said, hey, we're in great shape.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，通胀实际上仍然是一个问题，我们将提高利率，只是不是现在这一刻。

sentences.en: We've turned a corner.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This was a pause that said, let's make sure that we still have a banking sector in a year or so.
sentences.zh: 美联储并没有在这里宣布胜利。

sentences.en: And oh, by the way, inflation is actually still a problem and we are going to raise interest rates, just not this very moment.
sentences.zh: 所以总结一下，这就是我们目前所处的位置。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 通胀总体上已经下降了不少，但我们了解到，其中很大一部分，也就是我们感受最深的那部分，并非真正是美联储政策的结果，

sentences.en: The Fed was not declaring victory here.
sentences.zh: 这是一个需要理解的重要事实。

sentences.en: So in conclusion, here's where we are.
sentences.zh: 但吉娜，如果我是一个消费者，我真的会在意这种相对积极的情况是由什么引起的吗？

sentences.en: Inflation is down overall quite a bit, but we've learned that a lot of it, the stuff we feel the most, isn't truly the result of Fed policy,
sentences.zh: 通胀自去年夏天以来已经下降了一半。

sentences.en: which is an important thing to understand.
sentences.zh: 去杂货店购物不像以前那么糟糕了。

sentences.en: But Gina, if I'm a consumer, how much do I really care about what caused this relatively positive situation?
sentences.zh: 开车出行的经济负担也变得更容易承受了。

sentences.en: Inflation now down by half since last summer.
sentences.zh: 难道我不应该为这一切的发生感到高兴吗？

sentences.en: Grocery store shopping doesn't suck as much as it used to.
sentences.zh: 当然，你理应感到高兴。

sentences.en: Traveling by car financially is much more tolerable.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是消费者，你也不希望这只是暂时的。

sentences.en: Aren't I just pretty happy that all of this stuff has happened?
sentences.zh: 4%的通胀率比9%要好，但仍然不如以前的2%。

sentences.en: Sure, and reasonably you would be.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，你知道，这是需要记住的一点。

sentences.en: But if you're a consumer, you also don't want this to be temporary.
sentences.zh: 汽油价格现在下降了，但美联储无法控制它们，它们可能会再次上涨。

sentences.en: And 4% inflation is better than 9%, but it's still not as good as 2%, which is what it used to be.
sentences.zh: 经济中许多美联储只能在一定程度上控制的部分也可以这么说。

sentences.en: So I think that, you know, that's the thing to keep in mind.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么美联储如此专注于将通胀一路压低至其非常低且稳定的目标，并以一种更可持续的方式将其保持在那里。

sentences.en: Gas prices are down right now, but the Fed can't control them and they might rise again.
sentences.zh: 你想知道政策是有效的，而且是以你预期的那种方式有效。

sentences.en: And the same thing could be said for many parts of the economy that the Fed can only control somewhat.
sentences.zh: 而我们还没有完全达到那个目标。

sentences.en: And so that is why the Fed is so focused on wrestling inflation the whole way back down to its very low and stable goal and keeping it there in sort of a much more sustainable way.
sentences.zh: 没错，你肯定不想生活在一个因为运气好而导致通胀下降的世界里。

sentences.en: You want to know that policy is working and working in a way that you intend.
sentences.zh: 你希望它因为政策而可持续地下降，这样它才能真正保持在低位。

sentences.en: And we just aren't quite there yet.
sentences.zh: 是的，运气有好有坏。

sentences.en: Right, you really don't want to live in a world you're saying where your inflation goes down because of luck.
sentences.zh: 政策则要审慎得多。

sentences.en: You want it to sustainably go down because of policy so that it truly stays down.
